name: Four-lane arterial improvement — US preliminary design (FHWA case study, PD)

metadata.name: Clear Lake Avenue / Dirksen Parkway Improvements (Illinois DOT case study)
metadata.description: Improvements to roadways and intersections in a commercial area adjacent to the I-72/I-55 interchange at Springfield, audited at preliminary design stage together with a review of the existing roads, per the FHWA RSA Case Studies program.
metadata.scheme_summary: Access consolidation with two new service roads intersecting Clear Lake Avenue at a new signalized intersection east of Dirksen Parkway; dual left turn lanes on all legs of Clear Lake Avenue/Dirksen Parkway and dual right turn lanes on the southeast corner; Hill Street realigned to a new signalized intersection about 650 feet from the existing signals.

project_information_package.value: Preliminary design report: upgrade of Clear Lake Avenue between Dirksen Parkway and the I-72/I-55 interchange; access consolidation and construction of two new service roads intersecting Clear Lake Avenue at a new signalized intersection; realignment of Hill Street to a new signalized intersection; dual left turn lanes on all legs of Clear Lake Avenue/Dirksen Parkway and dual right turn lanes on the southeast corner.

design_drawings_current_phase.value: Plans of the planned improvements showing the realigned Hill Street, the new north and south service roads, additional left- and right-turn lanes, and the new signalized intersection.

crash_history.value: The intersection of Clear Lake Avenue and Dirksen Parkway was designated a high accident location for six consecutive years (1998 through 2003); the intersection of Hill Street and Clear Lake Avenue was designated a high accident location in 2003.

provenance.license: Public Domain (explicit ROSA-P rights metadata; 17 USC §105)
provenance.extractor: ORCH transformed FHWA-SA-06-017 Table 1 entry 'Illinois DOT: improvement to four-lane arterial road, preliminary design stage and existing roads' and the RSA Number 1 case study record (project background, TABLE A.1 selected safety issues and suggestions) into a Project input set; findings language patterned on the case study's summary-of-key-findings structure.

expected_findings_baseline.location: Clear Lake Avenue at the new south service road intersection, east of Dirksen Parkway
expected_findings_baseline.scenario: Queued, turning, and parking vehicles around the closely-spaced intersections of Clear Lake Avenue and the new south service road may interfere with each other on an approach corridor carrying recorded high-accident designations. Vulnerable road users acknowledged: pedestrians and cyclists may be present along this commercial corridor, but the identified conflict mechanism operates between queued, turning and parking vehicles, so road users are scoped to vehicle occupants.

statement.text: Check turning-restriction and parking-stall placement at the closely-spaced Clear Lake Avenue / south service road intersection so queued, turning, and parking vehicles cannot interfere with each other.

evidence.quote: Queued, turning, and parking vehicles around the closely-spaced intersections at Clear Lake Ave. and the south service road may interfere with each other.

confidence.label: medium
confidence.basis: Issue and location recorded for this scheme in FHWA case study TABLE A.1 (Issue 3).

expected_findings_baseline.rationale: ORCH-as-judge baseline derived from FHWA public-domain case studies; distinguishable from quoted evidence.
expected_findings_baseline.recommendation: Restrict turning movements and relocate the specified parking stalls clear of the functional area of the new south service road intersection.

expected_findings_baseline.location: New realigned Hill Street intersection with Clear Lake Avenue
expected_findings_baseline.scenario: The new signalized Hill Street intersection will sit about 650 feet from the signalized intersection of Dirksen Parkway and Clear Lake Avenue on a corridor with recorded high-accident designations; queues that do not clear between the close signals may spill back and block the upstream intersection. Vulnerable road users acknowledged: pedestrians and cyclists cross at both signalized intersections, but the identified mechanism (queue spillback between closely spaced signals) exposes vehicle occupants, so road users are scoped accordingly.

statement.text: Check queue storage between the new Hill Street signals and the Dirksen Parkway / Clear Lake Avenue signals and coordinate them so queues do not block the upstream intersection.

evidence.quote: The new signalized Hill Street intersection will be about 650 feet from the signalized intersection of Dirksen Parkway and Clear Lake Avenue.

confidence.label: medium
confidence.basis: Signal spacing recorded for this scheme in FHWA case study TABLE A.1 (Issue 1).

expected_findings_baseline.rationale: VRU acknowledgment carried explicitly; queue-spillback inference labelled as derived from the recorded spacing.
expected_findings_baseline.recommendation: Coordinate the adjacent signals and provide Do Not Block Intersection signs, with signing and signal displays enhanced for conspicuousness at the new intersection.

notes: Tier-0 snapshot to be recorded from actual deterministic run; baseline findings are judge targets, not engine outputs. Grounded in FHWA-SA-06-017 via ROSA-P (PD).
